source.title: Layer-wise Learning of Kernel Dependence Networks
source.authors: Chieh-Tsai Wu; A. Masoomi; A. Gretton; Jennifer G. Dy

page_placements.theme: Practical memorization and its generalization cost depend on model and procedure

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full workshop paper; it says this is part one of a full paper.
record.tranche_reason: Tests random-label fitting with KNet and same-size MLPs trained using MSE or cross-entropy, rather than reproducing the original study's setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports random-dataset training and test accuracies in Table 1. It does not report shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, Gaussian-noise-input, label-noise-fraction, regularization, or learning-order experiments.
record.test_reason: The SGD-trained MLP comparators measure fitting completely random labels in a new synthetic setting. Their training accuracies bear on V1, although chance performance and unchanged architecture or hyperparameters relative to true-label training are not established.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the relevant experimental passage: training accuracies are high, and the authors identify two random datasets as exceptions to generally good test accuracy. Their broader conclusion concerns greedy spectral optimization of KNet and evidence consistent with implicit regularization; they do not establish a matched random-versus-real-label generalization result.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses a synthetic Random dataset and compares a greedily trained kernel network with same-size MLPs trained by SGD using MSE or cross-entropy; it does not reproduce the original image-network settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Objective choice changes the reported random-dataset training accuracy: MSE is 0.98 ± 0.04, while cross-entropy is 1.00 ± 0.00.

fits_no_version.finding: Spectrally trained KNet achieves training accuracy 1.00 ± 0.00 and test accuracy 0.38 ± 0.21 on completely random labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A kernel dependence network trained greedily by spectral optimization can fit completely random labels.

record.problems: The Random dataset is synthetic rather than an image dataset. The text does not specify a test-set chance level. Table 1 is flattened in the supplied text, and reported metrics are means and standard deviations across 10-fold cross-validation.

untested.parts: Chance-level test performance and keeping architecture and training hyperparameters unchanged between true-label and random-label training are not established.

No matched comparison of true-label versus random-label fitting time or corruption-fraction convergence experiment. Timing comparisons across objectives and different datasets do not establish this claim.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise-input fitting experiments.
No sweep of label-corruption fractions measuring training and test error.
No controlled tests of weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation, or their removal.
No learning trajectories comparing acquisition of real patterns and memorization of noise.

record.verdict_notes: The Table 1 objective order is H, CE, MSE, and the record maps the Random dataset numbers correctly. The Adversarial dataset is designed around difficult class geometry, but the supplied text does not establish completely random labels there; its lower MLP accuracies therefore do not challenge V1.

versions.untested_parts: The text does not state that the random labeling is a permutation of labels over a particular image training set, and does not specify a chance test-accuracy baseline.
